entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Charleroi, a pivotal event in World War I, occurred on August 21, 1914, as the German army clashed with the French and British forces in Belgium. This 3-day battle marked the beginning of the Great Retreat, a 450-mile retreat of the Allied forces from the German advance. The battle's strategic location on the Meuse River made it a crucial test of the Allies' defenses, but they ultimately failed to hold their ground.

The Battle of Charleroi had significant consequences, as it allowed the German army to continue its push towards Paris and the eventual capture of the French capital. This led to the French government's decision to abandon Paris and move the seat of government to Bordeaux. The battle also marked the beginning of the end of the Schlieffen Plan, a key German military strategy that had been instrumental in their initial successes.

In the aftermath of the battle, the Allies regrouped and launched a series of counterattacks that would go on to shape the course of the war. The Battle of Charleroi serves as a reminder of the brutal reality of modern warfare and the devastating impact it had on civilians and soldiers alike.

As the French historian and military strategist, Charles de Gaulle, noted, 'The Battle of Charleroi was a turning point in the war, for it marked the beginning of the end of the German advance and the start of the Allied counterattack.'
